description: The only way to leave work running on its own: a named client flow with a trigger and results, and the cron that actually delivers it
client_copy: Lo que se repite queda armado como un flujo y anda solo.
_comment: IT DEPENDS ON kanban AND approval. Every run lands as a ticket, and a flow
that acts on the client's behalf goes through the approval gate like
anything else -- a scheduled job is not a licence to skip the yes.
THE ENGINE SURFACE IS THE promises GUARD, and it lives here as of phase 3b.
engine/promises/ (plugin.yaml + promises.py, a transform_llm_output hook) is
the one place in the kit that uses the ENGINE's own plugin system, and it is
flow's because what it checks is whether a flow the agent announced really
exists. WHERE IT LANDS ON THE AGENT DID NOT CHANGE: install.sh still writes
policy/plugins/promises/, the compose still mounts that at /opt/data/plugins
read only, and config.yaml's `plugins.enabled` still names it. The engine
reads its plugins from HERMES_HOME/plugins and knows nothing about this
registry; what moved is where the kit keeps the source.
THE CURATED FLOWS NOBODY ELSE OWNS LIVE HERE, under curated/ and not under
flows/, because they are not this plugin's own work: they are the catalog
of flows the product ships, and `flow` is the plugin that makes a flow a
thing at all. Each of the seven exercises only system skills -- approval,
deliverable, artifact -- or a base capability every agent has: answering
out of hours, the inbox summary, cases left open, a complaint, loading a
new customer, a report with its sources, the Monday web round-up. There is
no whatsapp-support or research plugin for them to belong to, and inventing
one to hold a FLOW.md would be a manifest with nothing behind it. If one is
ever written, the flow moves into it and this list gets shorter.
